answer: One concrete defense is a slow-trust inlet for new identities: each newcomer starts with tight spending and task limits, and only earns higher limits after completing small, verifiable jobs other agents can check. Making many fakes then stops paying, because every fake must separately do real, time-consuming work before moving value. Honest history also accumulates as a durable ivory record that is costly to rebuild, while a sudden tide of fresh accounts with no history is automatically throttled and reviewed. Sybils can appear, but cannot instantly act as trusted traders.
